# Digitakt II: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-13, research snapshot `dd6ecb49e2f2`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Full version. The brief one is [digitakt-2-brief.md](digitakt-2-brief.md).

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitakt II

- **C1** (C) One mod = one OS version. Addresses and stock bytes are version-specific (hash-pinned). A mod for Digitakt mk1 1.53 is refused on 1.54; Digitakt II 1.17 addresses do not carry to 1.18+. Porting = find every address again. Keep a separate build per OS version. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {digitakt2-perform}
- **C10** (C) Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers. Call stock routines in the emulator and compare with what they must return (complex-ping's check found that its SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply); measure one timing per project on the unit and carry the ratio (2x on the DT2 for DDR-reading code, 7-12x in one digimod case, a hard stop that overshot 3x as far). An emulator that agrees with itself proves nothing about silicon. The display is part of this: digikit's emulator showed intro frames upright that the panel showed upside down. Check one asymmetric picture on the unit before trusting the emulator's orientation. Incidents: [I36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x), [I37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i37-a-sharc-emulator-shifted-every-fractional-multiply), [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {digimod} {dn2-skill-md} The same holds for event fields: Modwerk read a knob's own push-button byte as FUNC, and an emulator reference screen lacked markers the unit draws. Incidents: [I55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i55-a-knobs-own-push-button-byte-was-read-as-func), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit).
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I70** A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller. Cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause. Fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes. Rules: A39.
- **I14** DAG registers stored through their own DAG hung the DSP. Cause: `DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar; the PRM forbids it and stock never does it. Fix: move DAG registers through an R register. Rules: A33.
- **I15** A frequency shifter froze the unit at boot. Cause: a selas defect left a nested hardware-loop end compressed; code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. Fix: `.NOCOMPRESS` around nested loops; cache write-back before running copied code. Ran on send and master 2026-10-30. Rules: A45,A28,A41.
- **I16** A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed the unit. Cause: the ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards. Fix: keep the decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes. Rules: A46.
- **I17** Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit. Cause: per-sample accesses to stock buffers in external DDR (`0x8045b3c0`). Fix: render into L2 and copy once per block. Rules: A52.
- **I18** The flash cave reportedly froze a unit at the logo. Cause: not settled ([CONFLICTS O18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md)). Fix: check the bytes the other cave users leave; prove the cave on a hard run. Rules: A43.
- **I23** Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at PREPARING. Cause: not stated; the author says not to assume the route is reliable everywhere. Fix: power cycle and the startup menu. Rules: A20,A36.
- **I27** An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip. Cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR). Fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly. Rules: A41,G9.
- **I80** A USB mode take-over left a Digitakt II off the bus until a power cycle. Cause: the stock mode switch stops the controller with no lock; most likely the detach never reached the line (the controller stopped while the external ULPI PHY was suspended or busy), or the PHY was left in a state the stock restart does not undo. The stock firmware writes no PHY register itself. Fix: digikit holds the restart for 2 s, parks the PHY's line (function control through ULPI_VIEWPORT) while the controller is stopped and spaces switches at least 3.5 s apart. That made the failure rarer, not absent, so the take-over is off by default since 2026-11-13; with USB CONFIG set to USB MIDI (no switch) the fast transfer was fully reliable. Rules: A55.
- **I36** The emulator undercounted DSP time by 2x to 12x. Cause: the emulators model no memory stalls. Fix: budget with silicon costs; leave a margin; measure once per project on the unit. Rules: A35,C4,C10.
- **I41** A label defined twice resolved to the wrong file. Cause: a label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object. Fix: unique label prefixes per file. Rules: D4.
- **I53** Boot-screen frames were upright in the emulator and flipped on the panel. Cause: the emulator decodes the intro bitmap as if the intro flush flipped like the main-UI blit. On the panel, intro rows are stored top-down mirrored. Why the intro path differs (flush routine or panel scan direction) is not established. Fix: digikit's `.dkbs` frames, safe screen and pixel helper use the panel's layout. The emulator decoder is not fixed yet. Rules: C10,D13.
- **I61** Odd jump targets froze a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator kept running. Cause: byte-aligned code sections put routines at odd addresses; a jsr/jmp to an odd address stops the ColdFire with an address error (vector 3), while the emulator keeps running. Fix: the linker refuses an odd-target absolute jsr/jmp into mod RAM; each code section starts with a 2-byte alignment. Rules: A42.
- **I67** Code built into .bss crashed a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator ran the zeros. Cause: two new routines were placed in `.bss` instead of the code section, so the unit jumped into zero-filled memory. The emulator executed the zeros as no-ops and booted. Fix: the routines are code again in 2.6.1. The README says not to flash a 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6 build; Digi2MacroOSC and Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM still name core 2.4. Rules: A42,C10.
- **I44** Recovery used on a Digitakt II after a crashing build; a cheap cable delivered nothing. Cause: the cable. Fix: rehearse recovery with your exact cable and the stock file. Rules: A11,A36.
- **I54** Safe mode by REC at power-on, tested on a Digitakt II. Cause: test. In the emulator, digikit's earlier queue scan missed the key (`safe:0`); reading the stock key state fixed it. On the unit, a key held at power-on does produce a report. Fix: — Rules: A29.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O20** DT2/DN2 stock intro frame rate: A) 30 Hz: digikit's PIT3 model (PCSR `0x093f`, PMR 8593), so the first scene table's 175 frames last 5.8 s (finding 117) B) 15 Hz: digikit's earlier emulator notes derive it from divisor 1024 (66.67 ms per frame; finding 07)
- **O18** DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` at boot: A) unusable: "digikit's flash_cave (0x403117c4) froze the device at the logo: that trailing region is not loaded or is cleared on the hardware, whatever the emulator does" (a comment in dt2-capicola's build script, vendored in dt2-machine-lab) B) usable: Deja Vu's releases put their payload there and were validated on a unit for boot and operation; 70b185's builds put a stub there and run on a unit; digikit's canary survived boot in its emulator
- **O7** Free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17: A) static: free up to `0x200fa000` (digikit finding 100) B) the owner's unit: clicks and delay leaks past `0x200f5a74`
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O24** Digitakt II NRPN numbers (OS 1.17): A) the OS 1.17 manual: track mute 1:101, track level 1:100, pattern mute 1:104, master overdrive 2:37, filter env depth 1:23, filter base/width 1:51/1:52, portamento 3:7/3:8 B) midi.guide's data: 1:108, 1:110, 1:109, 2:50, 1:26, 1:24/1:25, 3:6/3:7 (the mute and level numbers match the Digitone II's)
- **O25** Digitakt II LED colour byte (OS 1.17): A) digikit finding 19: the byte is a colour mask B) digikit finding 122: on a unit `0x31` shows deep blue and `0x41` yellow (one observer, by eye)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H2** (stock) Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once. Test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.
- **H3** (stock) A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid). Test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?
- **H5** (stock) Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01). Test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?
- **H19** (stock) The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20). Test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).
- **H24** (stock) The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too. Test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.
- **H25** (stock) The Digitakt II on OS 1.17 answers midi.guide's NRPN numbers (track mute 1:108, track level 1:110, pattern mute 1:109, master overdrive 2:50), not the manual's (1:101, 1:100, 1:104, 2:37) (O24). Test: On a throwaway project, send each NRPN pair from a DAW or a MIDI tool on the auto channel with value 0 and then 127, and watch which parameter moves on the screen.
- **H6** (probe) The DT2's SHARC DDR above the sample pool window (`0x9d22b9c8` up to `0xa0000000`, about 46 MB) is never written by stock, as the DN2's tail `0x80531000-0xa0000000` is not. Test: dnfw's method: fill the range with a pattern at boot, then scan it during heavy playback, pattern and kit changes, FX extremes, sample loads and a save. Expect a reserved top part for Capicola builds only.
- **H7** (probe) The DT2's ColdFire runs the same FreeRTOS layout as the DN2: higher priority numbers run first, prio 0 never runs, prio 1 is the idle loop; the main task's stack is barely used. Test: With the USB probe: find the ready table and the running-task pointer, sample them 60 times.
- **H9** (probe) The DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` is safe on a stock image; the freeze report (O18) came from something else in that build. Test: A stock image plus a canary in the cave, read back after a cold start after a long power-off (A40).
- **H14** (build) The SHARC's IIR0/FIR0 accelerators compute on the DT2 exactly as measured on the DN2 (output from stored word 5, FIR sums in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round). Test: Port the accelprobe image to the DT2 and compare the 76 result words.
- **H20** (build) DT2 OS 1.17 saves only the kits the user changed, so a module's own kit data that changes by itself is lost unless a stock parameter of that kit changes too. Test: Modwerk publishes a unit procedure: change only module data, save, power-cycle, reload.
- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T7** (needs unit + custom engine, effort L) Find the cause of the sticky "bitcrush until reboot"
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)
- **T14** (needs unit + emulator, effort M) Fix or document digikit's EMAC fractional-mode emulation against a unit measurement
- **T15** (needs unit, effort M) Probe free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17 between `0x200f5a74` and `0x200fa000` on a unit
- **T18** (needs files, effort M) Document the project file formats (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`) beyond song slots

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

- [doc] [hw] Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). - [doc] [hw] Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio} — `sysex-and-midi#1d9d72a8` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:132](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L132) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
- [hw] selache pitfalls that halt a real DSP but run in the emulator (elekloader ADAPTING.md, Nov 2026; the first matches 70b185's DT2 finding): A shift by a negative immediate (`LSHIFT R1 BY -16`) is encoded without sign extension. Put the count in a register (`R2 = -16; R1 = LSHIFT R1 BY R2;`). elekloader's lint flags candidates, but it cannot see instruction boundaries, so check each one in the listing. A C function whose locals sit more than ~63 words from the frame pointer is compiled wrongly. One large local array is enough. Keep large buffers static or in the voice state. `[hw]` {elekloader-adapting} {own-dt2-notes} — `toolchain-and-emulators#77b278df` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L18) · Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders

The PRM forbids it for Types 3 and 15. Stock loads such registers through their own DAG thousands of times but never stores one. The probe was `probe-samedag-store`, a single `DM(I4, M6) = M4` and no SIMD. - [hw] SIMD-mode loads and stores (the implicit PEy access at +4 bytes) into L2 byte space have no stock precedent: stock does SIMD data accesses only in L1 normal-word space, and SIMD stores to DDR at most. The manual allows them, but they are unproven on silicon. The shipping kernel does SIMD compute only and moves every load and store in SISD, toggling PEYEN per sample as stock does. Cost: 125,766 -> 31,472 instructions per block versus the C version. The full-SIMD version would have been 27,404. — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#46a44016` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L13) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. - [hw] L2 data is cached by a 16 KiB cache that maps lines 16 KiB apart to the same set. Buffers spaced at 16 KiB multiples thrash it, so pad or interleave them. Branches and calls are expensive: unroll small loops into hardware loops, avoid calls in per-sample code, and fill delay slots. — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#d0e8cba1` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L77) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. A task at priority 2-4 runs only after Audio finishes its block and is preempted by the next one, so it cannot make Audio miss a block. - [hw] `prvIdleTask` is at sw `0xb863ca` with no idle hook; its back edge is at sw `0xb863df`. `vTaskSwitchContext` sw `0xb85af7` stores `pxCurrentTCB` at sw `0xb85b6b`. Both are workable hook points for an idle counter or a task map, at ~250 device cycles per switch (~0.1 %). L2 code loads at byte `0x20000000` (sw `0xb80000`). "Audio" and "RPC" are created from internal-memory code (sw `0x1c3f6a`, `0x1c7775`). `[hw]` (hooks ran on the unit) — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#43f8592a` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:25](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L25) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. - [hw] A late block is always a whole missed block. Audio is locked to the block interrupt. If one block's work runs past the next interrupt, that interrupt is lost and Audio runs one block later: an exactly one-block dropout, never drift. `[hw]` — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#8d799445` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L28) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. - [hw] The stock engine governs its own per-block load. With 8 heavy stock tracks the Audio task ran at 99-100 % for whole 4 s windows and missed no block. Misses happen only when extra code inside the Audio task adds work the stock governor doesn't know about. So a custom engine must stop on a per-block deadline measured from the block start, with margin, not on an average budget. `[hw]` — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#9933bbf4` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L29) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. - [hw] Which words are free (DT2 1.17, measured): 670-676 arrive untouched. heavylight's engine uses 672-676. Words 1-6 are rewritten by the firmware after the block, so writes there never arrive. - [emu] [hw] Samples go to the DSP over link port 0 (LP0_CTL `0x30FFE000`; SEC sources 81/82/168), not over the frame link. LP1 is unused. One transfer is 0x401 words: a tag and 1,024 payload words. Tag `0xFFFFFFFF` means a slot header: slot, startL, startR, rate, len. Stereo means startL != startR. A tag below `0x19200` is a page number into the 400 MiB DDR sample pool at `0x8422B9C8`. This is the RPC-task work the owner saw while samples load. — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#b5c49fef` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:46](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L46) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. - [hw] Read-only USB SysEx probe in MAIN OS (heavylight's dt2-keyframer, derived from irpina/digihealth via dn2_firmware_explore): `F0 00 20 3C 7D 00 <pack7> F7`. Commands: HELLO 1 (returns word 0) and PEEK 3 (address, up to 256 bytes). There is no write command. It hooks the SysEx router at `0x40120006` (router `0x4011ffda`, header `0x4021e5d2`, send `0x40121d2a`, USB port 2), and the router itself drops device id 0x7D. It fits in 532 bytes of a free 896-byte run in MAIN OS 1.17 (`0x402e4f64`, `0x402e609c`) and coexists with Deja Vu V5.1, Musical V4 and Zoom V11. It also went into an elekloader-built image. It is built with plain binutils (`m68k-linux-gnu-as -mcpu=5475`). - [hw] A second SHARC stop on a real DT2: `fx/freqshift` on the send route froze the unit at boot; the emulator showed nothing (findings 77, 91). The last 11 instructions of every hardware loop must be 48-bit ISA, so wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS` ([rule A45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md)). Code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. WAVE 0-5 dispatch through a 6-entry table at `0x4022231c`; WAVE 6 is RAND. The table cannot be extended by appending: the RAND slew data sits right after it. The shared RNG is `(A,B) -> (B, A+B)` at `0x402b62c8/cc`. The phase increment is in D5 (signed); the stored phase is in D2. Raw WAVE 7/8 clamp to 6 and play RAND on stock. A parameter code maps to its array index through the descriptor table (rows of `0x3c` bytes, index as s32 at row + 4, -1 = no word); the same index means another parameter on another machine. - [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
- [doc] SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#aec8faff` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L90) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)

Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} — `memory-maps#c63308d3` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L18) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)

The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75} — `memory-maps#519a00ac` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L20) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm} — `memory-maps#40215568` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L22) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)

Shared ColdFire storage code: the block driver, the MmcFs slot store and the transfer routing; the sample filesystem, its request handler and the sample manager are DT2-only. `[doc]` {dn2-drive} — `memory-maps#22432990` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:23](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L23) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] eMMC card (both, about 32 GB part, 0x2E1A000 sectors assumed): sectors `0x0-0x457FFF` belong to the firmware (boot, tables, projects, pools, presets); MmcFs refuses writes at `0x457FFF` and above. DT2 1.17: factory sample table "MaGj" at `0x458000` and 1,265 factory samples to `0x5D7FFF` - never touch; +Drive (ekFS) `0x5D8000-0x2DF017F`; `0x2DF0180` to the end unused. DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. Unchecked bank ids in the Data API can reach every sector below `0x800000` over USB - put any private store above that line (digikit: DT2 `0x2DF1000+`, DN2 `0x800000+`). Not checked on a real card. `[doc]` {digikit-f59} — `memory-maps#501b88cc` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:24](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L24) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)

- [doc] Two protocol generations: the Digitakt II / Digitone II speak "gen-2"; Analog Four speaks "gen-1" with a different pattern format and a slower wire. `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio} — `sysex-and-midi#87fc4dba` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:14](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L14) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
- [doc] The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#7642b2b0` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L35) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)

A DN2 answered only `0x15` in a sweep and ignored `0x0B-0x0E`, `0x14` and `0x16`. The same bytes appear in the OS files ([`firmware-container.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} Three different device ids. - [doc] Elektroid reads the product id from byte 5 of the decoded `Device` (Ping) reply and looks it up in its device table; digi-roll captured 42 and 43 from a DT2 and a DN2 the same way. The FAQ table on elektron.se (Heat `000A`, Digitakt `000C`, Digitone `0014`, Heat MKII `0016`, Model:Samples `0019`, Model:Cycles `001B`, Digitone Keys `001C`) matches Elektroid's table entry for entry, so that table lists product ids. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {digi-roll-protocol} {elektron-faq} — `sysex-and-midi#a82f614a` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L55) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Elektroid's further product ids: Analog Four `0x04`, Analog Keys `0x06`, Analog Rytm `0x08`, Analog Four MKII `0x0E`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x10`, Syntakt `0x1E`. Overwitch's Overbridge ids: Analog Four MKII `0x0B47`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x0B48`, Digitone Keys `0x0B35`, Syntakt `0x0B4A`. digikit read the DT2's USB ids from the image: `0x012B` (USB MIDI), `0x102B` (audio/MIDI), `0x0B2B` (Overbridge), so the low byte is shared across modes. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {overwitch-devices} {digikit-f42} — `sysex-and-midi#5388b9cc` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L56) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Unpacked request body: `seq_hi seq_lo 00 00 type payload...`. The two bytes after seq must be `00 00`. A non-zero byte there and the unit never replies. — `sysex-and-midi#26a2be46` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:79](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L79) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] Unpacked reply: `counter16 seq16 (type|0x80) payload...`. The first pair is a device-side counter, not the seq; the echoed seq is the second pair. — `sysex-and-midi#23194457` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:80](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L80) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The whole body is 8-in-7 packed, one collector per 7 bytes. Short bodies (Ping, `ReadDir /`) look unpacked, which misled early tools. Longer payloads must be packed or the unit answers "Invalid path". — `sysex-and-midi#9b9d3eba` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L81) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] All integers are big-endian, strings are NUL-terminated (< 256 bytes), and no checksum is used. — `sysex-and-midi#fe5d9257` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:82](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L82) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] No wire-controlled memory read or write exists over MidiRpc. Eight surfaces were audited (Data partial R/W, path resolvers, FsRaw, the backup streams, the route table, the full type factory). Live RAM is not reachable this way; the OS-upgrade path writes flash only. `[doc]` — `sysex-and-midi#869c11db` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:106](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L106) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The factory debug console is on UART8, not MIDI: `#HELLO`, `#READ`/`#WRITE` (an 11-name parameter table, not memory), `#DUMP_AUDIO`, `#ENTER_TEST_MODE`, `#MRAM_DUMP` (a fixed 13.8 MiB factory/calibration blob, magic "COKi"), `#MMCDUMP` (raw eMMC sectors). It is not known to be reachable from outside. Agents: leave it alone. `[doc]` — `sysex-and-midi#cdad2325` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:108](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L108) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The same screen request works on more devices: Elek View, a browser port of screendump that sends the request in the `F0 00 20 3C 10 00` RPC framing, was tested on a Digitakt II and a Model:Cycles, and its author reports an Analog Heat MKII working too. So the Heat MKII speaks this RPC framing; whether the Heat +FX does is a stock test (HYPOTHESES H18). `[doc]` {elek-view} — `sysex-and-midi#bde6941b` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:116](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L116) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II specifics and client pitfalls (dnfw `midi-rpc.md`, live on a DN2 1.11)

Decompress-recompress scripts round-tripped projects that then loaded on DN2, DT2, M:S and M:C (forum post, no log); the compression is LZ4 according to syxgrid's author. `[doc]` {em-dx2-scripts} — `sysex-and-midi#d0e282a7` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:117](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L117) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II specifics and client pitfalls (dnfw `midi-rpc.md`, live on a DN2 1.11)
- [doc] The panel MCU sends 2-byte packets on UART8: key packet: `0x20 | channel`, then the channel's 8-bit button mask; encoder packet: `0x30 | (encoder-1)`, then a signed 8-bit delta; high nibble 7: the factory console. — `sysex-and-midi#8472cf05` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:120](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L120) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Key code = `channel*8 + bit + 1` (codes 1-48, plus a few exceptions per device). There are nine encoders. — `sysex-and-midi#97f65e08` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:124](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L124) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Toward the panel: `B9 idx val` sets an LED to a palette entry, `B5 i r g b` sets a palette entry. — `sysex-and-midi#bcfe4cfd` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:125](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L125) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Connectors: `system` (local computer, for format conversion), `elektron`, `cz`, `sds`, `efactor_preset`. Elektron filesystem families: raw/sample (`raw`, `preset-raw`, `sample`), data (`data`, `project`, `preset`, `preset-takt-ii`, `sound`), memory (`ram`, `track`). The Digitakt II "Preset" filesystem is implemented as `preset-takt-ii`. `raw` and `data` are for testing only and not compatible with Transfer formats. A firmware `upgrade` command exists in the CLI (which devices is not stated). Device definitions come from `~/.config/elektroid/elektron/devices.json` if present. Elektron samples cannot be swapped. `[doc]` {elektroid-readme} — `sysex-and-midi#dcc899c9` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:163](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L163) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Elektroid (dagargo) - a general sample/SysEx client

- [doc] digikit (current home ElekLabs/digikit, `[doc]` {digikit}): native Rust emulator running ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together with front panel, display and audio; web panel (WASM) and Tauri desktop app; `patchkit` applies modules to the user's own `.syx` and refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8; headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes; control socket for patch injection; ColdFire/DSP analysis databases and Ghidra tooling. Targets: Digitakt II 1.17 (also runs 1.16; 1.15C for old analysis), Digitone II 1.12 (also runs 1.11; 1.10E for old analysis). Caveats: DSP not real-time yet; browser host parked on `wip/browser-host`; no patched firmware installed on a device by the author; bootstrap-menu recovery untested on hardware. AGPL-3.0-or-later with NOTICE terms asking for the credit "digikit by Em D". — `toolchain-and-emulators#936e3acb` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:50](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L50) · Toolchains and emulators / Emulators
- [doc] Earlier digikit README (m-dwyer/digikit, {digikit-old}) described a Python/Unicorn design: ColdFire emulator for Digitakt II / Digitone II; patched Unicorn m68k (SR read, CCR sync, EMAC MAC with load; stock Unicorn refused); ColdFire-aware disassembler because Capstone misses MVS/MVZ and FF1; first run needs a cold boot of a few minutes to build snapshots; about 10M instructions/s. Works: core, interrupt controllers, PIT, DMA timers, eDMA, front-panel TX, display, SD/MMC up to identification. - [doc] Stock Unicorn 2.1.4 (and QEMU master as of 2026-09-15) gets ColdFire wrong in ways that change results (emu-elektron's patch notes) `[doc]` {emu-elektron-patches}: Condition codes: they are committed lazily, so a hook or a counted stop in mid-block sees stale flags, and the next branch goes the wrong way. MAC/MSAC with load is decoded wrongly in four ways: Ry with bit 0 or 1 set faults as "dual accumulate" on a CFV4E; Rx is always D2; MSAC adds instead of subtracting (this also hits MSAC without load); MASK is applied to every load address. The DT2 main OS reaches one of these at `0x400db9e0`. EMAC fractional and signed arithmetic is wrong (as found by SyntHack and octabam). EMAC saturation with MACSR.OMC gets its sign and constants wrong. Any ColdFire emulator built on Unicorn needs these fixes before its audio or branch results mean anything. emu-elektron carries all of them as patches for five devices. — `toolchain-and-emulators#f0b75153` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L83) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] Calling convention: a delayed `CALL` with a frame; arguments in R4, R8, R12, more on the stack; result in R0. Most kernels come as a pair: `reset(record)` and `process(record, in, out, n)`, one 32-sample block per call. - [doc] The ColdFire <-> SHARC frame is the same shape as on the Digitone II: A full-duplex `0xabc`-byte DSPI2 frame carries a `0x802`-byte state payload: 16 records of `0x60` bytes, track n to SHARC unit n. ColdFire eDMA29 sends and eDMA28 receives; the SHARC uses SPI2 with completed-image double buffering. The send is driven from a level-5 interrupt that a level-6 eDMA-completion path forces in software. Link settings: SPI mode 1, 16-bit MSB-first, one `0x55e`-word window. The meaning of the SHARC-to-ColdFire return content is open. Compare the DN2's frame and reply words in [digitone-2-internals.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md). This is a second, independent reading of the shared design (research map T19). — `digitakt-2#fc3a7acd` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:111](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L111) · Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)

- [doc] Reading a track's Sound parameter words needs no fixed address: get the project singleton, its ProjectSettings at project + `0x30` (static analysis only), the selected track from `view_track` (clamped 0-15), then `native_track_sound(active kit, track)` = kit + `0x6c` + `0x3c0` x track; vtable slot `0x28` of that Sound object returns the record pointer `*(sound + 0x10)` (0 when none is bound), and word i is a big-endian s16 at record + `0x14` + 2i. Anchors: settings `0x40041d18` (DT2 1.17) / `0x4003e40e` (DN2 1.12); `native_track_sound` `0x40035cca` / `0x40030e66`. The array holds 71 words on the DT2 and 101 on the DN2. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#2f9dd954` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:171](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L171) · Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
- [doc] Track overdrive (stock): the curve clamps to +-1 and applies y*(2-|y|) three times; the blend is x + mix*(y-x) with stock ramps for drive and mix. OVR Routing is parameter `0x103` (Sound mirror index 68; 0 = pre, `0x100` = post). The per-track stage is called twice per track from the voice chain. `[doc]` {digikit-overdrive} — `digitakt-2#b6a530b4` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:173](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L173) · Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
- [doc] Run-time machines: on the DT2 they can use knob slots B C E F G H; a parameter on the seventh slot replaces LEV, whose level is then fixed at 100. The run-time module stage is limited to 64 KB; a TB-303 port costs about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block. `[doc]` {digikit-tb303} — `digitakt-2#7e9747d1` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:174](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L174) · Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
- [doc] The firmware's own file calls can write samples: open (`0x40158902`, mode "w"), write (`0x4015866a`), reserve, hash (`0x4015b3aa`), close (`0x401588c0`), info, delete (`0x40157078`), mkdir and rename (`0x40156f6c`, which keeps the inode, size and stored hash). Each takes the recursive filesystem mutex itself and blocks, so call them from a task, never an interrupt. The sampler's recorder `0x40153c70` is a complete stock caller. `[doc]` (static) — `digitakt-2#236ea41c` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:179](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L179) · Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
- [doc] Open does not truncate: an existing file opens at position 0 with its old size and data; stock deletes first. Whole 32 KiB pages at multiples of `0x8000` are written straight from the buffer, the rest goes through the page cache. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#1e9e4d84` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:180](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L180) · Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
- [doc] Power cut: a cut mid-write leaves a visible file with a partial size and no hash; the mount was not seen to repair it. Delete refuses an open file (open-file bitmap at `0x46f4ded0`). Only `/factory` is RAM-backed; user files always go to the card, and a failed card write is not reported. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#3eabeb87` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:182](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L182) · Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
- [doc] In RAM: the project object is at `0x41776c9c`; 128 patterns from `0x41776cb8` (stride `0x1db8c`), 128 kits from `0x426532b8` (stride `0x5574`). Serializer `0x400df66c` (flag bits pick the parts), loader `0x400df95a`. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#139eedc4` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:186](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L186) · Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
- [doc] Sites: encoder filter `0x40111cda`; per-frame value block `0x80005b50`; modulator call site `0x4002e90c`; LED frame `0x4003117c`, LED setter `0x400308e0`; NameView wrapper `0x40117c70`. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#b7490ff8` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:191](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L191) · Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
- [doc] USB mode switch: `FUN_40006c16` has the same address and bytes on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. It takes no lock and cuts a MIDI reply in flight; USB restarts after a 30-tick counter (about 1 s in the emulator; counter DT2 `0x40965a38`, DN2 `0x4058f280`). The stored USB CONFIG byte (0 MIDI, 1 Overbridge, 2 AUDIO/MIDI; DT2 `0x4099d5c4`, DN2 `0x405ce898`) is written only by the menu actions (DT2 `0x4010331a`/`30`/`48`, DN2 `0x40104dc2`/`d8`/`f0`), never by the switch, so a reboot returns to the stored mode; an Overbridge disconnect (`FUN_400f2ce0`) is the only path that re-applies it by itself. DT2 connection-state word `0x40965a40`. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#bf9d1341` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:195](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L195) · Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] +Drive internals: close hash `0x4015b1e8` under the filesystem mutex `0x46f4deb0` (recursive lock `0x400015a0`, unlock `0x400016d2`); inode get/put/write `0x4015b92a`/`0x4015b846`/`0x4015b868`; extent lookup `0x4015813c`; hash-table rebuild `0x4015b0ee` (about 300 ms per file on a unit); event post `0x4015a6aa`. Data page 0 is card sector `0x5ee180` (page p at base + p x `0x40`), the first hash page sector `0x5ee980`. Every file write reaches the card before the call returns. The eSDHC read/write is clamped to 64 KiB (DT2 `0x4012e3c4`, DN2 `0x4012ca8a`). `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#62df9041` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:197](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L197) · Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] SHARC cycle counter: each image has exactly one EMUCLK reader, the block handler (DT2 `0x1c74cd`, DN2 `0x1c9d6b`), which keeps a low-word delta for reporting only; nothing branches on it. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#efc4e61f` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:200](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L200) · Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] eMMC EXT_CSD copy in RAM: DT2 1.17 `0x4fe69100`, DN2 1.12 `0x4e6f9100`; bytes are reversed within each 32-bit word because the eSDHC runs little-endian. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#507f758b` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:201](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L201) · Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] External ULPI PHY: the USB controller drives an external ULPI PHY (PORTSC.PTS = ULPI, set at init `0x40006d1c`-`0x40006d2c`). The stock firmware writes no PHY register: its only ULPI_VIEWPORT (`0xFC0B0170`) use is a read of PHY register 0 every 300 calls of a periodic function (`0x40006af8`), which resets the controller (not the PHY) when the read never finishes. It never sets PORTSC.PHCD. The VBUS interrupt (`0x40005e14`, OTGSC.BSVIS) starts or stops the controller; the restart `0x40006bc6` starts it only while OTGSC.BSV is set. Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#df260dc9` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:205](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L205) · Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
- [doc] Stock card driver: data moves by eDMA channel 59 to the eSDHC data port, 16 bytes per request; every write uses CMD23 with the reliable-write bit. The block write and read split every transfer into 64 KiB commands: `cmpi.l #0x10000,D2` at offset 0x14 (entry) and 0x22 (chunk loop) of each function, same bytes on both images: DT2 1.17 read `0x4012e1b6` (sites `0x4012e1ca`, `0x4012e1d8`), write `0x4012e39c` (sites `0x4012e3b0`, `0x4012e3be`); DN2 1.12 read `0x4012c87a` (`0x4012c88e`, `0x4012c89c`), write `0x4012ca60` (`0x4012ca74`, `0x4012ca82`). The 64 KiB bounce buffer for unaligned buffers is the likely reason; the eDMA's 15-bit count allows at most 1023 blocks (511 KiB) a command, which digikit's sdhc-large uses (1022) for 16-byte aligned buffers it registers. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2#7dd73593` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:207](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L207) · Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
- [doc] +Drive ids at or above `0x1000000` never reach the card (DT2 1.17): the inode write-back `0x4015b868` and page write-back `0x40155c34` call the block write only for inode ids and page numbers below `0x1000000`; higher ones are copied into RAM tables (inodes at `0x47d73ed0 + n*0x80`, pages at `0x46f63ed0 + n*0x8000`, n counted from `0x1000000`). `[doc]` {digikit-f120} — `digitakt-2#c199ed2e` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md:210](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md#L210) · Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
